verdict.rationale: Logseq is documented as privacy-first and local-first, and syncing is an opt-in, per-graph choice, so a user can keep any graph only on their own device. Community users also confirm data stays local. However, nothing shows that users can choose a region or residency for data stored in Logseq Sync's cloud, and third-party sync setups such as Syncthing, iCloud or git are user workarounds that earn no credit. Missing for 10: region/residency selection for Logseq Sync storage, documented data-location details for synced graphs, independent corroboration of residency controls.
